deities: Sage Parshuram (tirtha of his penance); the site is a sacred bathing kund on the Lohit river rather than a conventional temple shrine
festivals: Parshuram Kund Mela on Makar Sankranti (mid-January), when thousands of pilgrims take a holy dip in the kund

history.period: Mythological origin; modern mela facilities developed in recent decades
history.summary: TIRTHA, NOT A CONVENTIONAL TEMPLE: Parasuram Kund is a sacred bathing site (kund) on the lower Lohit river within the Kamlang Reserve Forest, Lohit district, rather than a built temple complex. Hindu legend holds that sage Parshuram washed away the sin of matricide in the waters here at Brahmkund (the Lohit is the Brahmaputra's upper course), a story linked in sources to the Kalika Purana, Srimad Bhagavat and the Mahabharata; the kund is ringed by dense forest of sacred rudraksha trees. Each year on Makar Sankranti (14 January) thousands of pilgrims from across India converge for the Parshuram Kund Mela to bathe in the icy waters. DISTANCE DISCREPANCY (verify): older sources say the kund is ~3 miles (or 13 miles) north-east of Tezu; a recent travel guide puts Tezu to Parshuram Kund at ~46-50 km (1.5 hours), with Tinsukia ~150 km and Dibrugarh ~200 km away. Coordinates are approximate (geocoder matched only at district/region level near Wakro). The CSV town 'Tezu' is acceptable as the nearest town/headquarters, though the site is a rural river gorge, not in Tezu town itself.

name: Parasuram Kund
town_description: Tezu is the headquarters of Lohit district in eastern Arunachal Pradesh, on the right bank of the Lohit river. It is the gateway town for Parshuram Kund and for the Mishmi Hills region, with a small domestic airport (TEI) and road links to Tinsukia and Dibrugarh in Assam via the Bhupen Hazarika Setu bridge.
tradition: Hinduism (tirtha - sacred bathing site, not a built temple)

travel.airport: Tezu Airport (TEI, ~50 km, limited scheduled flights); most visitors use Dibrugarh Airport, Assam, then drive via Tinsukia and Tezu.
travel.railway: Tinsukia Junction (Assam), about 150 km away, is the nearest major railhead; Dibrugarh is another option.
travel.road: About 13 miles (~21 km) north-east of Tezu by older accounts, or ~46-50 km per a recent guide (discrepancy flagged); reached by road via Wakro; state buses run Tinsukia-Tezu, and private taxis are the usual last leg.

visitor_information.best_time: November to January, peaking at the Makar Sankranti mela (mid-January); expect severe cold. Summer and monsoon visits are possible but the river is rough.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open site with no fixed temple hours; bathing ghats accessible through the day during the mela period (verify locally).
